A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fair Clustering via Alignment by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FCA/FCA-C experiments on tabular datasets, visual clustering, and synthetic data, including ablations and runtime measurements in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results on CREDITCARD, three protected groups, additional comparisons, and coupling-solver sensitivity.

M1.justification: The central alternating FCA/FCA-C procedures remain. v3 adds an evaluated Sinkhorn-based alternative for coupling optimization in C.3.7. Algorithm 2 also revises the written FCA-C cost on W from v1's transport cost ci,j to CK-means, aligning that step with the stated objective; this does not establish that the original implementation changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds CREDITCARD evaluation and a BANK scenario with single, married, and divorced protected groups (Table 4), whereas v1 evaluates BANK with two groups. These extend existing tabular fair-clustering coverage; the original tabular, image, and synthetic tasks remain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 8 adds Chierichetti et al. (2017) to the ADULT/BANK/CENSUS comparison alongside SFC and FCA. v3 also directly compares FCBC with FCA-C at similar cost in Table 7. The original tabular and visual baseline sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds silhouette evaluation, an ADULT comparison targeting Cost approximately 0.314, and a Sinkhorn regularization sweep. C.1 removes capital-loss from ADULT's stated feature list, resolving v1's inconsistency between '5' features and six listed variables. This revises the reported specification but does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new C.3.7 ablation tests how replacing linear programming with Sinkhorn and varying regularization affects utility, fairness, and runtime. The approximately cost-matched FCBC comparison and silhouette analysis provide additional targeted checks. Existing partition-size, initialization, optimization, scalability, and K-median analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-initialization coefficient-of-variation reporting and five-run runtime means and standard deviations are unchanged: v1 Tables 11, 13, and 14 correspond to v3 Tables 16, 18, and 20. The new experiments do not introduce additional uncertainty-reporting practices or stated run-count increases.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and experimental plots are retained, but new results substantially broaden the evidence across multi-group fairness, comparator coverage, alternative utility measurement, CREDITCARD, and solver sensitivity. For example, v3 Table 7 reports FCA-C Cost/Bal of 0.313/0.473 versus FCBC's 0.314/0.443; Table 11 reports FCA's CREDITCARD result of 0.402/0.653. These are added comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: A.4 extends the Lp-norm upper-bound argument to distances satisfying triangle inequality, translation invariance, and homogeneity. The principal proofs remain substantively unchanged. The explicit tau + 2 approximation bound, 3R epsilon additive term, and boundedness assumption highlighted in v3 Theorem 4.3 already appeared in v1 Theorem B.3.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: objective decomposition, FCA/FCA-C, approximation guarantees, favorable fairness–utility trade-offs, and numerical stability. The additional evidence supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3's Impact Statement explicitly limits the work to proportional fairness, distinguishing individual fairness and fairness in group clustering costs. New discussion explains why clustering cost alone may be insufficient and recommends linear programming after observing Sinkhorn's tuning sensitivity and modest runtime savings.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an FCA implementation-repository link absent from v1, clarifies the ADULT feature specification, and documents the added experiments' settings, including CREDITCARD preprocessing provenance and Sinkhorn regularization values. Existing hardware, libraries, iteration budgets, and core hyperparameters remain documented as before.

R1.justification: v3 adds Schmidt et al. (2019) and Yeh and Lien (2009) to the references. New Remark 4.4 compares the stated approximation guarantees with Bera et al. and Schmidt et al. The broader positioning relative to fairlets and pre-, in-, and post-processing approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes local wording and explanatory revisions, moves the deterministic-assignment remark from the appendix to Remark 3.4, combines the optimization and initialization appendix subsections, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The boxed algorithm descriptions become numbered pseudocode, Figure 2 gains clearer protected-group labels, and six additional tables display the new experiments. Existing table designs and Figures 1 and 3–9 are retained, with relocation and renumbering rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the empirical assessment through the approximately cost-matched FCBC comparison, multi-group validation, additional utility measurement, and solver ablation. The implementation link and explicit fairness limitations also improve usability and interpretation. These are useful incremental gains: the central guarantees, original benchmark results, and uncertainty reporting remain essentially unchanged.
